goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — workingHours.find rejects a slot if ANY range sharing that weekday excludes it, so split shifts or UTC-midnight-split hours (e.g. organizer at UTC-10, 09-17 local -> 19:00-24:00Z + 00:00-03:00Z) lose all slots in the second range.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `workingHours.find(...)` to reject a slot if it is outside *any* `workingHour` range that matches the weekday (`workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())`). With multiple ranges on the same weekday (split shifts / UTC-midnight-split hours), a slot that is valid in one range but invalid in another will still be rejected because `.find` returns true on the first excluding range. This matches the finding’s described failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find returns true on the first same-day override that excludes the slot, so a day with multiple override ranges (e.g. 09-11 and 14-16) rejects every slot in the later ranges.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` when the slot is outside a same-day override window (e.g., `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end)... )`). Because `find` stops at the first match, a day with multiple override ranges will reject valid slots in later ranges: for a slot at 14:00 and an earlier override 09–11, the 09–11 override makes `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` true, so `find` returns true and the function returns `false` (slot unavailable) before considering the 14–16 override. This behavior is directly implied by the new logic around lines ~99–150 in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — Working-hours end check uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so a 60-min slot starting at 16:30 with hours ending 17:00 passes.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — Comparing two dayjs objects with === is always false, so the zero-length (day unavailable) override branch is dead and a slot starting exactly at the override instant is treated as available.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Override-day matching keys on UTC calendar date of the override start (and server-local format vs utc slot), so an override spanning UTC midnight (e.g. 14:00-20:00 at UTC-7) misses the post-midnight slots, which fall back to regular working hours instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, overrides are only considered for slots whose UTC day matches `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,"minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` (and `slotStartTime` is forced to `.utc()`). This effectively keys an override to a single calendar day derived from the override *start*, so if an override’s time window spans into a different UTC date (e.g., an afternoon/evening override in a negative offset timezone that crosses UTC midnight), slots on the later UTC date won’t match the `format("YYYY MM DD")` equality and `dateOverrideExist` stays false, causing the code to fall back to the normal `workingHours` check instead of applying the override window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:214 — Shifting override minutes by the invitee-organizer offset with hour()/minute() wraps past midnight (UTC-7 organizer 09-17 seen from UTC+6 gives start 1320, end 360), yielding an inverted frame and dropping or corrupting override slots.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new override conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` as `dayjs(override.start|end).utc().add(offset,"minute").hour()*60 + ...minute()`, i.e., “minutes within the day” after applying the invitee-organizer offset. This drops any day rollover when the offset pushes the time past midnight. In such cases `endTime` can become numerically less than `startTime` (e.g., shifting a daytime range forward across midnight), producing an inverted override window that the downstream logic (which expects start/end minutes in a single day range) can mis-handle, effectively corrupting or dropping overrides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:206 — activeOverrides is still selected by the override's wall-clock-as-UTC start falling in the invitee's day, so for large offsets an override applies to the adjacent invitee day while its shifted times belong to another day.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes how `activeOverrides` entries are converted into minute-of-day ranges (adds offset adjustment) in `packages/lib/slots.ts`. It does not show how `activeOverrides` is *selected/filtered by day* in the first place, so the claim that it is “still selected by the override's wall-clock-as-UTC start falling in the invitee's day” cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/types/schedule.d.ts:5 — Shared TimeRange adds timeZone as optional, but getSlots (packages/lib/slots.ts:212) now depends on it; any caller passing overrides without timeZone silently gets dayjs.tz(undefined), which falls back to the server local zone and gives the wrong override offset.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/slots.ts, getSlots now computes organizerUtcOffset via `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. In the same diff, TimeRange’s `timeZone` was added as *optional* (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), so `override.timeZone` can be `undefined` at runtime for any caller that constructs overrides without it. The new offset math (`inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`) would then be based on whatever `dayjs.tz` does with an undefined zone (likely default/local), producing incorrect adjusted `startTime`/`endTime` minutes for overrides. The diff does not add a guard/default in getSlots, so this is a correctness risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — Working-hours check uses `find` to reject if ANY same-day range excludes the slot, so users with multiple ranges per day (or a local day split across two UTC ranges) lose valid slots.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours logic rejects a slot if `workingHours.find(...)` returns any same-day range where `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime`. With multiple working-hour ranges on the same day, a slot can be inside one range but outside another, and this code will still find the excluding range and return `false`, incorrectly dropping valid slots. This behavior is directly in the diff (the `workingHours.find` block around slots.ts ~139).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slot end, so slots that run past the end of working hours are not rejected.
matched_golden_ids: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of the slot’s end time, which is the same incorrect end time calculation described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — Override upper bound checks slotStartTime.isAfter(end), so slots that start inside the override but end after it (and slots starting exactly at end) are accepted.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the date-override exclusion logic only treats a slot as outside the override when `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end)... )` (and when `slotEndTime` is <= start). There is no check that `slotEndTime` is <= override end, so a slot that starts within the override window but ends after `date.end` will not trigger the `dateOverrides.find(...)` early return-false path and will be accepted (via `dateOverrideExist` => `return true`). Also, a slot starting exactly at `date.end` is not considered outside because `isAfter` excludes equality, so it will be accepted as within the override.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — Comparing two dayjs objects with `===` always yields false, so a zero-length (unavailable all day) override never blocks the day through this branch.
matched_golden_ids: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug as the golden comment: using `===` to compare two dayjs objects compares references (not date/time values) and therefore will not work as intended, affecting the zero-length override logic. It aligns with the golden recommendation to use value comparison (e.g., `.isSame()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Override day-matching formats `dayjs(date.start)` in server-local time but slotStartTime in UTC, and only looks at the start date, so overrides crossing UTC midnight or running on a non-UTC server get matched to the wrong day.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the override-day match compares `slotStartTime` (explicitly `time.utc()`) against `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format(...)`, but `dayjs(date.start)` uses the server-local timezone interpretation of the `Date` object (no `.utc()`/`.tz()`), making the day comparison depend on server TZ and potentially mismatching UTC days. Also, the logic gates override applicability on the (shifted) start date matching the slot’s day (`format("YYYY MM DD")` check), so an override spanning midnight won’t apply to slots on the following day. Both behaviors are directly implied by the new `dateOverrides.find(...)` block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:221 — Shifting override start/end by the invitee-organizer offset and then taking hour/minute wraps around midnight, which can give endTime < startTime (or 0) and break the computed availability for that day.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the override minutes are computed as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()*60 + ...` (same for end). This converts a shifted timestamp to “minutes-from-midnight” while discarding the shifted date. If `add(offset)` crosses a day boundary, the hour/minute will wrap (0–23), so an override that is logically later/earlier can end up with `endTime < startTime` (or otherwise mapped to the wrong part of the day). The subsequent logic treats `startTime`/`endTime` as an intra-day range when unsetting working hours, so this can break availability computation for that day.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — New working-hours rejection branch in checkIfIsAvailable (with the start==end bug at line 142) has no test exercising slots outside working hours.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` a new working-hours gate was added. Inside it, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` exactly like `start` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), rather than using the slot end (e.g., `slotEndTime`). This means the code cannot correctly reject slots that start within working hours but extend past `workingHour.endTime` (and the branch is new in this diff). The added test covers date-override timezone behavior, not slots outside working hours, so this logic is currently unexercised by tests in the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — Full-day-unavailable override branch (start===end compared by object identity, never true) has no test, so the dead comparison went undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new date-override logic includes `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) { return true; }`. This compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference identity, which will never be true, so the intended “start equals end” (full-day/unavailable or special-case) branch is effectively dead. The added test covers a timezone/date-override scenario in `getSchedule.test.ts` but does not exercise this equality case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788 — Only added case uses Asia/Dhaka (+6:00) vs Asia/Kolkata (+5:30), both non-DST positive offsets; no negative-offset, DST-transition, or midnight-spanning override coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new timezone-offset adjustment logic for date overrides (e.g., in `packages/lib/slots.ts` and `checkIfIsAvailable` using `utcOffset()`/offset math). The only newly added test case in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` covers a positive, non-DST offset change (`Timezones["+6:00"]` vs an existing `+5:30` context), and does not exercise edge cases that the new logic could mishandle (negative offsets, DST transitions, or overrides that span midnight). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap for the newly introduced nontrivial timezone logic, not a proven defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:792 — New +6:00 test reuses the +5:30 day-window (18:30Z) instead of the invitee's local midnight, so it does not really verify invitee-timezone day boundaries.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added test sets `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` but still uses a day window of `startTime: ${plus1DateString}T18:30:00.000Z` to `endTime: ${plus2DateString}T18:29:59.999Z`. 18:30Z corresponds to local midnight for +5:30, not +6:00 (which would be 18:00Z to 17:59:59.999Z). So the test likely does not actually validate invitee-timezone day boundary behavior for +6:00; it mostly reuses the prior offset window and asserts the same UTC slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:211 — Rewritten override offset math in getSlots (organizer vs invitee offset shift) has no direct unit test in slots tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites date override handling in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (lines around the `activeOverrides` mapping) to compute an `offset` from organizer vs invitee timezones and adjusts start/end via `dayjs(...).utc().add(offset, "minute")`. The only added test shown is in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts`, which is an integration-style `getSchedule` test, not a focused unit test for `getSlots`/`slots.ts`. From the diff, there is no new/updated test file targeting `packages/lib/slots.ts` directly, so the review point about missing direct unit coverage for this nontrivial logic is grounded (though there is some indirect coverage via `getSchedule`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:576 — Per-user organizerTimeZone for round-robin/loose hosts and differing host timezones is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new per-user `organizerTimeZone` plumbing for availability checks in multi-host cases (e.g., `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule.timeZone` / `userSchedule?.timeZone` when filtering slots for loose/fixed hosts around ~lines 489, 514, 576). The only added test covers a date override with a different invitee timezone in `getSchedule.test.ts`, but it does not exercise round-robin/loose-host scenarios or differing host timezones. That makes the review concern (untested new per-user timezone behavior in those branches) concrete and diff-grounded, though not a proven runtime defect by itself.
